newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel blasts Annan's U.N. settlement report.
newsitem.headline: Israel blasts Annan's U.N. settlement report.

text.p: Israel on Sunday blasted U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan's report criticising the Jewish state's construction of a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"This report will join a long list of one-sided United Nations documents on the Arab-Israeli conflict. This report again proves that the U.N. cannot play a role as an honest broker in the peace process," the foreign ministry said in a statement.

Annan's report said Israel's building of Har Homa settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim between Jerusalem and PLO-ruled Bethlehem "appears to represent, in the view of the Palestinian people, the largest single negative factor in the breakdown of the peace process".
"Palestinian communities in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, including Jerusalem, have responded with two months of public demonstrations and protest."
The report was requested by an emergency special session of the General Assembly in April which demanded the immediate cessation of construction at the site.

The Assembly resolution, adopted by a vote of 134 to three with 11 abstentions, also demanded a halt to all other Israeli settlement activities and called for an end to all support for "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.

Israel, which captured East Jerusalem along with the West Bank in 1967, says it has the right to build where it likes in the city it claims as its united capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem for capital of a future state.
Annan's report backed the Palestinian view that the settlement was aimed at preempting future peace talks on the city's fate.

The report said the construction begun in March "represents the first move to construct an entirely new settlement on occupied Palestinian lands since a freeze was imposed on such activities by the previous Israeli government". The Palestinian U.N. observer mission has declared its intention of calling for the reconvening of the emergency Assembly session.
Israel said the emergency session which requested Annan's report was a waste of the world body's resources.

"The fact it is convened raises astonishment given the many important and serious issues on the internartional agenda which do not get the attention they deserve in the United Nations," the foreign ministry said.
The statement urged the world to reject the report and to instead call on the Palestinians to restore direct negotiations with Israel.
